sections.content:
UP only changed the HUD bar. DOWN had no changes at all (no output in the "CHANGES from DOWN" section). So UP/DOWN don't seem to do anything meaningful to the gameplay.
Let me reconsider the game. So far I've found:
- MOUSE on purple block: only changed HUD
- SPACE (first time): split the white block, top half became purple
- SPACE (second time): only changed HUD (no effect on blocks)
- LEFT: rotated the purple block in gray frame to diamond
- RIGHT: rotated it back
- UP: only changed HUD
- DOWN: no changes at all
The only meaningful gameplay change was the first SPACE which split the white block. And LEFT/RIGHT rotate the framed block.
Wait - maybe I need to click on different things to select them, then use arrow keys to move them. Or maybe I need to click on the top-right palette blocks first.
Let me try clicking on the white block in the top-right palette (the small white 3x3 block), then see what happens.
Actually, let me reconsider. The target is ~55 actions. That's a lot. Maybe I need to:
1. Select a color from the palette
2. Click on cells to paint them
3. Build the target pattern
Or maybe the game is about moving a cursor around and painting cells one by one.
Let me try clicking on the white block in the top-right panel (around row 4, col 37).

sections.label: TOOL CALL: python
sections.content:
<tool_call>
<function=python>
<parameter=code>
# UP/DOWN don't affect gameplay. Let me try clicking on the palette blocks in top-right.
# The white 3x3 block is at rows 3-5, cols 36-38
# The purple 3x3 block is at rows 3-5, cols 42-44

print("Probing: click on white palette block (row 4, col 37)")
result = action([{'action': 'MOUSE', 'row': 4, 'col': 37}])
print("Result:", result)

# Check changes
before = last_transition.before_frame.segmentation
after = last_transition.after_frame.segmentation
before_nodes = {n['id']: n for n in before['nodes']}
after_nodes = {n['id']: n for n in after['nodes']}

print("\n=== CHANGES ===")
changed = False
for nid in sorted(set(list(before_nodes.keys()) + list(after_nodes.keys()))):
    bn = before_nodes.get(nid)
    an = after_nodes.get(nid)
    if bn is None or an is None or bn['pixels'] != an['pixels'] or bn['boundary'] != an['boundary'] or bn['color'] != an['color']:
        changed = True
        if bn is None:
            print(f"  Node {nid} appeared: color={an['color']}, pixels={an['pixels']}")
        elif an is None:
            print(f"  Node {nid} disappeared: color={bn['color']}, pixels={bn['pixels']}")
        else:
            print(f"  Node {nid}: color {bn['color']}->{an['color']}, pixels {bn['pixels']}->{an['pixels']}")
            if bn['boundary'] != an['boundary']:
                print(f"    boundary: {bn['boundary']} -> {an['boundary']}")
if not changed:
    print("  No changes")
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
